investigationPlans.projectUnderstanding: Sentry v1.0.2 (npm name qa-platform) is a local-first AI QA desktop application shipping for Windows 11 x64 + WSL2 (Ubuntu preferred), built as a pnpm 9.12.3 / turbo monorepo (Node >=22, TypeScript, React renderer, Vitest; 175 test files) with three apps (apps/desktop main/preload/renderer, apps/cli packaged CLI, apps/runtime Linux runtime) and 17 packages. The Linux runtime owns the canonical SQLite repository, managed project copies and immutable revisions (ProjectManager), frozen snapshot manifests with per-entry sha256 and deterministic walk order (SnapshotEngine), disposable per-AgentRun isolated workspaces (WorkspaceFactory: reflink-preferring copyTree with 'inert-unsafe' symlink policy and a .sentry-workspace/baseline-hashes.json index), the execution lease (RuntimeInstanceLease, 5s heartbeat / 20s stale), and the RunCoordinator. Desktop/CLI reach the runtime only via typed stdio NDJSON RPC; renderer IPC and the external CLI share desktop-command-router validation with a narrower external allowlist. One, two or three agents (OpenCode, DeepSeek, GLM via Claude Code) independently investigate the same immutable snapshot and each returns findings, evidence, usage and events which the coordinator validates and persists with provenance (agentRunId, sourceAgentStackId, snapshot provenance); merger/verifier/issue/retest components are retained historical compatibility (retests still invoke them internally) and are not active Desktop QA stages. Security posture: safeStorage-backed provider credentials with no plaintext fallback, credentials excluded from renderer payloads, memory-only runtime configuration, durable cancellation, boot recovery that interrupts stale lease owners while preserving findings/evidence, RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED reconciliation for RPC timeouts, and no silent retries that could duplicate paid runs. Run instructions are null in the mission context, so README.md and docs/ (architecture contract v1-pipeline.md, threat model, WSL maintenance boundary) are the authoritative behavioral specification for this investigation; the immutable snapshot is the code under test. Dependencies (node_modules) are absent in this snapshot, so executing the suite may be infeasible and source-level verification may be required.
criticalFlows: Project import: source selection (skips common generated caches, does not evaluate .gitignore) → managed copy + immutable revision via ProjectManager → frozen snapshot manifest/content hash via SnapshotEngine.

QA run start (Full and Targeted share topology): preflight resolves only selected stacks → project locking, revision integrity check, snapshot freeze → initial QARun persisted before the frozen hook (retest foreign keys) → TargetSpec frozen/validated against the snapshot manifest and persisted before agents start.

Concurrent independent agent execution: WorkspaceFactory creates a disposable private workspace per AgentRun from the frozen snapshot (baseline hash index written outside the agent-visible tree) → harness adapters own provider transport, sessions, tool restrictions, event/usage translation and child-process disposal → coordinator validates and persists events, derived activities, findings and evidence with provenance.

Evidence pipeline: containment/trust checks, evidence grounded to originating AgentRun, operation and snapshot provenance; durable artifact bytes and repository records must survive disposable workspace cleanup; agent agreement cannot upgrade evidence strength.

Run lifecycle outcome aggregation: handled pre-execution errors terminalize the persisted row; settled workers produce completed/partial/failed/cancelled parent outcomes; unavailable credentials, missing prerequisites and malformed output become structured failures; partial output and peer outcomes must not disappear.

Durable cancellation and shutdown: cancellation is a persistent control request acknowledged by the runtime owner, who signals owned adapters, waits for settlement/disposal and workspace cleanup, then records completion; pending retest cancellation propagates to the child run; no new adapters start after a pre-execution cancellation; shutdown refuses active QA/retests.

Runtime lease and boot recovery: heartbeats establish ownership; recovery interrupts work whose owner is stale, preserves findings/evidence, releases abandoned locks, and reconciles persisted active runs (RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED) without inventing completion or creating a second run.

Desktop↔runtime boundary: typed stdio RPC carrying serializable requests/responses/bounded updates only; renderer IPC and external CLI share desktop-command-router validation with a narrower external allowlist; runtime dispatch separately validates start options/IDs.

Credential and secret handling: OS-backed safeStorage encryption of provider settings in the Desktop main process with no plaintext fallback, credentials excluded from renderer payloads and exports/logs, runtime configuration memory-only.

Exports and historical compatibility: JSON/log exports retain historical merge/verification/issue sections; runs.get returns historical merge/verification data; retests invoke merge/verification services internally after independent target QA.
WSL maintenance and recovery: optional WSL disk reclamation requires explicit confirmation and administrator consent; managed-data deletion on project removal preserves imported originals.
weakPoints: WorkspaceFactory.cleanup parent-deletion heuristic (packages/workspace-factory/src/index.ts:78-88): when the resolved path ends in workspace/project it deletes the parent directory — brittle naming coupling that can delete too much or too little, and the whole rm -rf rests on resolveInside(dataRoot, ...) being airtight.

RuntimeInstanceLease error handling (packages/persistence/src/runtime-lease.ts:60-100): heartbeat failure is only latched inside the autoHeartbeat interval callback, the timer keeps firing with no backoff or stop, and assertHealthy depends solely on the latched error; races between the 20s staleness window and long filesystem operations could allow double ownership or premature boot-recovery interruption of a live owner.

Symlink classification and copy TOCTOU (packages/persistence/src/filesystem.ts:89-125, 209-263): internal/external classification uses realpath at scan time and can diverge from copy time; internal symlinks are recreated inside agent workspaces; symlink snapshot hashes cover scope+target string, not target content, so snapshot integrity can miss content drift at link targets.

Freeze/copy consistency gap: manifest scan, baseline-hash index generation and workspace copyTree are separate passes over the working copy — concurrent modification can make workspace bytes diverge from the frozen manifest that TargetSpec validation and evidence provenance trust.

Coordinator complexity concentration: packages/run-engine/src/index.ts (1534 lines) plus retest-service.ts (1111) and verification-service.ts (987) concentrate lifecycle ordering, outcome aggregation, cancellation propagation and historical merge/verify compatibility — the most likely location for ordering, double-terminalization or lost-partial-outcome defects.
RPC-timeout reconciliation: the RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED path in apps/runtime must not invent completion or create a second run; timeout-vs-actual-start races need code-level verification.

Test-coverage asymmetry: apps/desktop has 48 unit test files while workspace-factory has 1, snapshot-engine 1 and persistence 6 — thin coverage around exactly the containment/path-validation code the security claims rest on.

Shared command router drift: renderer IPC and the external CLI share desktop-command-router with a 'narrower allowlist' — allowlist or argument-validation drift between the two surfaces could expose runtime commands or IDs to the external CLI.

Documented security guarantees not yet code-verified: 'no plaintext persistence fallback' (safeStorage unavailable path), 'credentials stay outside renderer payloads', export/log redaction, and memory-only runtime configuration are claims in README/threat model requiring failure-path verification.

Dependency availability: node_modules is unpopulated in this snapshot, so running the Vitest suite may be infeasible and verification may have to rely on reading test sources instead of executing them (limitation to record).
plannedChecks: Read packages/run-engine/src/index.ts end-to-end and verify lifecycle ordering: QARun persisted before the frozen hook, TargetSpec persisted before agents start, handled pre-execution errors terminalize the persisted row, and settled workers aggregate to completed/partial/failed/cancelled without losing partial peer outcomes or double-terminalizing.

Trace durable cancellation through coordinator and apps/runtime/src/runtime.ts: owner acknowledgement, adapter signalling, settlement/disposal, workspace cleanup, completion record; confirm pending retest cancellation propagates to the child run, no adapters start after a pre-execution cancellation request, and shutdown refuses active QA/retests.

Audit packages/workspace-factory/src/index.ts cleanup against packages/persistence/src/paths.ts (resolveInside, agentWorkspacePath): path-escape attempts and cases where the workspace/project basename heuristic deletes the wrong directory or leaves data behind.

Audit packages/persistence/src/filesystem.ts copyTree/walkTree/copySymlink for symlink escape and abort semantics: partial-copy cleanup on failure, the concurrency/Promise.race scheduling, 'wx' flag collision when a workspace is recreated after rm(workspaceRoot), and divergence between classify-time realpath and copy-time link state.

Verify freeze→baseline→copy agreement: that baseline-hashes.json matches actual workspace bytes, and that snapshot restore/artifact-store paths (packages/snapshot-engine, packages/persistence/src/artifact-store.ts) validate manifest relativePath against traversal and symlink entries.

Inspect RuntimeInstanceLease usage in apps/runtime/src/runtime.ts: heartbeat failure latch/backoff/stop semantics, the 20s stale threshold versus long filesystem operations, and boot recovery that interrupts stale owners while preserving findings/evidence and releasing abandoned locks without inventing completion.

Review packages/evidence-pipeline containment/trust checks: provenance fields on findings and evidence, durability of artifact bytes across workspace cleanup, and enforcement that agent agreement cannot upgrade evidence strength.

Verify desktop-command-router allowlist parity between renderer IPC and apps/cli (external commands narrower; runtime dispatch validates start options/IDs), including validation of run/project IDs and start options before dispatch.

Audit the credential flow in apps/desktop: safeStorage-unavailable failure path (no plaintext fallback), exclusion of credentials from renderer payloads and from JSON/log exports, and the memory-only runtime configuration claim.

Inspect harness adapters (packages/harness-opencode, harness-deepseek, harness-claude-code) for child-process disposal on cancel/failure, usage/token accounting, tool-restriction enforcement, and structured failures on malformed model output.

Cross-check documented boundary suites (Full/Targeted, parallel, cancellation, recovery, export, issue/retest, sandbox in apps/runtime/tests and packages/run-engine/tests) against the weak points above and record concrete coverage gaps, especially for workspace-factory, snapshot-engine and persistence.

Attempt test execution (pnpm/turbo run test) only if dependencies can be resolved in the sandbox; otherwise record the inability to execute tests as a limitation and complete verification by reading test and product sources.

investigationPlans.projectUnderstanding: Sentry is a local-first AI QA desktop application (v1.0.2) in a pnpm monorepo. Windows Electron desktop owns presentation, provider settings, and runtime connection while a Linux/WSL runtime owns SQLite persistence, managed project copies, immutable revisions/snapshots, leases, and agent coordination. Selected agents (OpenCode, DeepSeek, GLM via Claude Code) run independently against disposable workspaces copied from a frozen snapshot and emit validated harness events (plans, findings, evidence, usage) that are persisted and exported as JSON/log. Historical merger/verifier/retest compatibility is retained but is not an active Full/Targeted QA stage.
criticalFlows: Project import -> managed working copy -> immutable ProjectRevision -> run-start ProjectSnapshot with streamed NDJSON manifest and content hash.
QA run lifecycle: lock managed copy, select stacks, persist QARun, create per-agent isolated workspaces, run planning/investigation/reporting, persist findings/evidence/usage, export JSON/log.
Harness protocol sequence validation and operation correlation across adapter-agnostic events.
Targeted QA: validate TargetSpec against the frozen snapshot manifest, then execute only focused paths with full-strength independent agents.
Cancellation and crash recovery: durable cancellation requests, runtime leases, stale-owner recovery, workspace cleanup without losing persisted outputs.
Desktop/runtime boundary: typed stdio RPC, safeStorage-backed credentials, host path translation, and update fan-out.
weakPoints: Generated TypeScript build artifacts are shipped: *.tsbuildinfo files (including apps/desktop/tsconfig.preload.tsbuildinfo and packages/shared/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo) are present despite .gitignore. In a clean checkout they make tsc -p skip emit or emit partial dist, so pnpm build/pnpm test fail until the tsbuildinfo files and dist directories are removed.

Full test suite is not green on this WSL host: harness-claude-code/tests/qa-prompt-parity.test.ts fails with run.failed/GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE because the adapter's WSL mount-isolation preflight runs and fails closed on a WSL host without a systemd user bus; the test does not stub wslMountIsolationOverride, so it is environment-dependent.
Repository hygiene gate cannot run from the supplied snapshot because no Git repository metadata is present; pnpm repository:check exits 1 on git ls-files.

Developer/agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md) require running 'shux contract', but no shux executable is shipped or available; docs/development/ui-command-center.md acknowledges this.

Desktop build has a coupled post-build script (scripts/fix-preload.mjs) that fails when tsc skipped preload emit; the root cause is the stale tsbuildinfo, but the script gives only an ENOENT on dist/preload/package.json rather than a clear build-order diagnostic.
Windows distribution relies on an online Linux runtime bootstrap and an unsigned ZIP without an automatic updater or signed installer; this is documented but remains a supply-chain/update weakness.

tool bash result: # Sentry

Sentry is a local-first AI QA desktop application. OpenCode, DeepSeek, and GLM
through Claude Code independently investigate one immutable project snapshot
and return findings, evidence, token usage, and persistent run history.

**[Sentry v1.0.2 — Windows Stable](https://github.com/Mert1026/Sentry/releases/tag/v1.0.2)**
supports **Windows 11 x64 with WSL2**, with Ubuntu preferred. The unsigned ZIP uses
an online Linux runtime bootstrap. Native Linux Desktop is deferred.

## Install and start

Use the PowerShell download/install block on the stable Release page to obtain
the Windows ZIP and matching SHA256 sidecar from any working directory.
[Verify the checksum and extract into a new directory](docs/setup/distribution.md),
then run from the extracted archive:

```powershell
.\sentry.ps1 version
.\sentry.ps1 setup -Distro Ubuntu
.\sentry.ps1 tools -Distro Ubuntu
.\sentry.ps1 open
```

Windows Node/pnpm/Git are not required for packaged Desktop. WSL setup requires
standalone Linux Node >=22, pnpm **9.12.3**, systemd user services, bubblewrap and socat.
Prerequisites can require manual administrator actions and a reboot. There is no
automatic updater or signed installer. See [getting started](docs/getting-started.md)
and the [installation and maintenance guide](docs/setup/distribution.md).

Successful setup registers the per-user command. Open a new PowerShell or
Command Prompt window and use `sentry open`, `sentry stop`, `sentry status`,
`sentry doctor` or `sentry version` from any folder. Keep the extracted archive
in place; after moving it, run `.\sentry.ps1 register-command` there.

New imports skip common generated caches and environments. Source selection does
not evaluate `.gitignore`; data directories remain eligible. Existing revision
hashes stay compatible. See [project imports](docs/setup/distribution.md#project-imports).

```text
AgentStack = Model + Harness + Execution Requirements + QA Policy

```

The stack is the unit the QA Core schedules: one `AgentRun` = one stack × one
task inside one `QARun`. The domain reasons about stacks generically — there is
no `if (model === 'opencode')` anywhere; vendor specifics belong in adapters.

`ExecutionSafeguards` contains operational controls only: `runTimeoutMs` and
`commandTimeoutMs`. They are process safety boundaries, not product quotas.

was “Muse QA Agent” (`stack_muse_main`, adapter `muse-code`); old rows stay
readable and are never rewritten to the new stack id.

plan.projectUnderstanding: Sentry is a local-first AI QA desktop application (v1.0.2) in a pnpm monorepo. Windows Electron desktop owns presentation, provider settings, and runtime connection while a Linux/WSL runtime owns SQLite persistence, managed project copies, immutable revisions/snapshots, leases, and agent coordination. Selected agents (OpenCode, DeepSeek, GLM via Claude Code) run independently against disposable workspaces copied from a frozen snapshot and emit validated harness events (plans, findings, evidence, usage) that are persisted and exported as JSON/log. Historical merger/verifier/retest compatibility is retained but is not an active Full/Targeted QA stage.
criticalFlows: Project import -> managed working copy -> immutable ProjectRevision -> run-start ProjectSnapshot with streamed NDJSON manifest and content hash.
QA run lifecycle: lock managed copy, select stacks, persist QARun, create per-agent isolated workspaces, run planning/investigation/reporting, persist findings/evidence/usage, export JSON/log.
Harness protocol sequence validation and operation correlation across adapter-agnostic events.
Targeted QA: validate TargetSpec against the frozen snapshot manifest, then execute only focused paths with full-strength independent agents.
Cancellation and crash recovery: durable cancellation requests, runtime leases, stale-owner recovery, workspace cleanup without losing persisted outputs.
Desktop/runtime boundary: typed stdio RPC, safeStorage-backed credentials, host path translation, and update fan-out.
weakPoints: Generated TypeScript build artifacts are shipped: *.tsbuildinfo files (including apps/desktop/tsconfig.preload.tsbuildinfo and packages/shared/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo) are present despite .gitignore. In a clean checkout they make tsc -p skip emit or emit partial dist, so pnpm build/pnpm test fail until the tsbuildinfo files and dist directories are removed.

Repository hygiene gate cannot run from the supplied snapshot because no Git repository metadata is present; pnpm repository:check exits 1 on git ls-files.

Developer/agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md) require running 'shux contract', but no shux executable is shipped or available; docs/development/ui-command-center.md acknowledges this.

Desktop build has a coupled post-build script (scripts/fix-preload.mjs) that fails when tsc skipped preload emit; the root cause is the stale tsbuildinfo, but the script gives only an ENOENT on dist/preload/package.json rather than a clear build-order diagnostic.
Windows distribution relies on an online Linux runtime bootstrap and an unsigned ZIP without an automatic updater or signed installer; this is documented but remains a supply-chain/update weakness.

finding.title: Clean builds and tests fail from the supplied snapshot because generated tsbuildinfo files are shipped
finding.description: The snapshot ships generated TypeScript incremental metadata (`*.tsbuildinfo`) even though .gitignore excludes it. In a clean checkout, `tsc -p` trusts this stale metadata and skips emitting outputs that are absent from the checkout. Observed effects: packages/shared build exited 0 with no dist; packages/schemas produced only primitives.js and no index.js; apps/desktop preload tsc exited 0 with no dist/preload, causing fix-preload.mjs to fail with ENOENT; apps/cli and apps/runtime dist were absent after a forced turbo run. Deleting the tsbuildinfo files and rebuilding emits the missing dist outputs.
finding.expectedBehavior: A clean checkout of the snapshot should run pnpm build and pnpm test without requiring manual deletion of ignored generated artifacts.
finding.actualBehavior: tsc exited 0 but dist was missing or partial, causing build/test failures (TS2307 for @qa/shared or @qa/schemas and ENOENT for dist/preload/package.json) until tsbuildinfo files were removed.
reproductionSteps: Run `pnpm run build` in packages/shared with the shipped tsbuildinfo (op_13) and observe no dist emitted.
Run `npx tsc -p tsconfig.preload.json` in apps/desktop with the shipped tsbuildinfo (op_40) and observe no dist/preload emitted.
Delete the tsbuildinfo files and rebuild (op_19, op_41, op_78, op_82) to observe the missing dist outputs are emitted.
finding.rootCause: The snapshot packages generated TypeScript incremental metadata (`*.tsbuildinfo`) that is ignored by .gitignore. In a new path, tsc -p trusts this metadata and skips emitting outputs that are absent from the checkout.
finding.recommendedFix: Exclude `*.tsbuildinfo` and `dist` artifacts from published snapshots, and add a packaging/pre-build check that fails when ignored generated files are present.

finding.title: Claude Code QA prompt parity test is not hermetic on WSL hosts without a systemd user bus
finding.description: The qa-prompt-parity test constructs ClaudeCodeHarnessAdapter with the `windowsUsersRoot` test seam but does not set `wslMountIsolationOverride`. On this WSL2 host, the adapter's WSL mount-isolation preflight runs and fails closed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any provider turn, so the last adapter event is `run.failed` and the assertion expects `run.completed`. A focused vitest run reproduces the failure, and a node reproduction of the adapter without the override emits run.failed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE and makes 0 prompts. This is correct runtime fail-closed behavior, but the test is environment-dependent.
finding.expectedBehavior: The parity test should pass on any supported host by stubbing the WSL mount-isolation preflight.
finding.actualBehavior: The focused vitest run reports `expected 'run.failed' to be 'run.completed'`; the adapter emits run.failed with code GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any provider prompt.
reproductionSteps: Run `pnpm --filter @qa/harness-claude-code exec vitest run tests/qa-prompt-parity.test.ts` (op_86); it reports 1 failed test.
Run a node reproduction of the adapter without wslMountIsolationOverride (op_51); it emits run.failed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any prompt.
finding.rootCause: The adapter correctly fails closed when WSL mount isolation is unavailable, but the parity test only stubs `windowsUsersRoot`, not `wslMountIsolationOverride`; on WSL hosts without a systemd user bus the preflight fails before the test's clientFactory is used.
finding.recommendedFix: Add `wslMountIsolationOverride: { status: 'available', reason: 'test-seam' }` to the ClaudeCodeHarnessAdapter options in qa-prompt-parity.test.ts (or otherwise stub the WSL preflight) so the test is host-independent.

finding.title: Repository hygiene gate fails when the snapshot has no Git metadata
finding.description: `pnpm repository:check` invokes `git ls-files --cached`. The supplied snapshot contains no .git directory, so the script prints `Repository hygiene check could not inspect tracked files.` and exits 1. The gate cannot be used to validate the QA snapshot as delivered.
finding.expectedBehavior: The repository hygiene check should either run in a Git checkout or report not_run/not_applicable when no Git metadata exists.
finding.actualBehavior: `pnpm repository:check` printed `Repository hygiene check could not inspect tracked files.` and `EXIT:1`.
reproductionSteps: Run `pnpm repository:check` (op_69); it prints the failure and `EXIT:1`.
finding.rootCause: The check assumes a Git working tree, but the QA snapshot is a source archive without .git metadata.
finding.recommendedFix: Run repository hygiene only in Git checkouts, or provide a snapshot mode that skips git-dependent checks and reports not_run.

finding.title: Agent instruction files reference unavailable shux command
finding.description: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md instruct users or agents to run `shux contract`, but no shux executable is shipped in the repository or available on PATH. This is already acknowledged in docs/development/ui-command-center.md.

finding.recommendedFix: Remove or replace the `shux contract` instruction in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md.

plan.projectUnderstanding: Sentry v1.0.2 (npm name qa-platform) is a local-first AI QA desktop application shipping for Windows 11 x64 + WSL2 (Ubuntu preferred), built as a pnpm 9.12.3 / turbo monorepo (Node >=22, TypeScript, React renderer, Vitest; 175 test files) with three apps (apps/desktop main/preload/renderer, apps/cli packaged CLI, apps/runtime Linux runtime) and 17 packages. The Linux runtime owns the canonical SQLite repository, managed project copies and immutable revisions (ProjectManager), frozen snapshot manifests with per-entry sha256 and deterministic walk order (SnapshotEngine), disposable per-AgentRun isolated workspaces (WorkspaceFactory: reflink-preferring copyTree with 'inert-unsafe' symlink policy and a .sentry-workspace/baseline-hashes.json index), the execution lease (RuntimeInstanceLease, 5s heartbeat / 20s stale), and the RunCoordinator. Desktop/CLI reach the runtime only via typed stdio NDJSON RPC; renderer IPC and the external CLI share desktop-command-router validation with a narrower external allowlist. One, two or three agents (OpenCode, DeepSeek, GLM via Claude Code) independently investigate the same immutable snapshot and each returns findings, evidence, usage and events which the coordinator validates and persists with provenance (agentRunId, sourceAgentStackId, snapshot provenance); merger/verifier/issue/retest components are retained historical compatibility (retests still invoke them internally) and are not active Desktop QA stages. Security posture: safeStorage-backed provider credentials with no plaintext fallback, credentials excluded from renderer payloads, memory-only runtime configuration, durable cancellation, boot recovery that interrupts stale lease owners while preserving findings/evidence, RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED reconciliation for RPC timeouts, and no silent retries that could duplicate paid runs. Run instructions are null in the mission context, so README.md and docs/ (architecture contract v1-pipeline.md, threat model, WSL maintenance boundary) are the authoritative behavioral specification for this investigation; the immutable snapshot is the code under test. Dependencies (node_modules) are absent in this snapshot, so executing the suite may be infeasible and source-level verification may be required.
criticalFlows: Project import: source selection (skips common generated caches, does not evaluate .gitignore) → managed copy + immutable revision via ProjectManager → frozen snapshot manifest/content hash via SnapshotEngine.

QA run start (Full and Targeted share topology): preflight resolves only selected stacks → project locking, revision integrity check, snapshot freeze → initial QARun persisted before the frozen hook (retest foreign keys) → TargetSpec frozen/validated against the snapshot manifest and persisted before agents start.

Concurrent independent agent execution: WorkspaceFactory creates a disposable private workspace per AgentRun from the frozen snapshot (baseline hash index written outside the agent-visible tree) → harness adapters own provider transport, sessions, tool restrictions, event/usage translation and child-process disposal → coordinator validates and persists events, derived activities, findings and evidence with provenance.

Evidence pipeline: containment/trust checks, evidence grounded to originating AgentRun, operation and snapshot provenance; durable artifact bytes and repository records must survive disposable workspace cleanup; agent agreement cannot upgrade evidence strength.

Run lifecycle outcome aggregation: handled pre-execution errors terminalize the persisted row; settled workers produce completed/partial/failed/cancelled parent outcomes; unavailable credentials, missing prerequisites and malformed output become structured failures; partial output and peer outcomes must not disappear.

Durable cancellation and shutdown: cancellation is a persistent control request acknowledged by the runtime owner, who signals owned adapters, waits for settlement/disposal and workspace cleanup, then records completion; pending retest cancellation propagates to the child run; no new adapters start after a pre-execution cancellation; shutdown refuses active QA/retests.

Runtime lease and boot recovery: heartbeats establish ownership; recovery interrupts work whose owner is stale, preserves findings/evidence, releases abandoned locks, and reconciles persisted active runs (RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED) without inventing completion or creating a second run.

Desktop↔runtime boundary: typed stdio RPC carrying serializable requests/responses/bounded updates only; renderer IPC and external CLI share desktop-command-router validation with a narrower external allowlist; runtime dispatch separately validates start options/IDs.

Credential and secret handling: OS-backed safeStorage encryption of provider settings in the Desktop main process with no plaintext fallback, credentials excluded from renderer payloads and exports/logs, runtime configuration memory-only.

Exports and historical compatibility: JSON/log exports retain historical merge/verification/issue sections; runs.get returns historical merge/verification data; retests invoke merge/verification services internally after independent target QA.
WSL maintenance and recovery: optional WSL disk reclamation requires explicit confirmation and administrator consent; managed-data deletion on project removal preserves imported originals.
weakPoints: WorkspaceFactory.cleanup parent-deletion heuristic (packages/workspace-factory/src/index.ts:78-88): when the resolved path ends in workspace/project it deletes the parent directory — brittle naming coupling that can delete too much or too little, and the whole rm -rf rests on resolveInside(dataRoot, ...) being airtight.

RuntimeInstanceLease error handling (packages/persistence/src/runtime-lease.ts:60-100): heartbeat failure is only latched inside the autoHeartbeat interval callback, the timer keeps firing with no backoff or stop, and assertHealthy depends solely on the latched error; races between the 20s staleness window and long filesystem operations could allow double ownership or premature boot-recovery interruption of a live owner.

Symlink classification and copy TOCTOU (packages/persistence/src/filesystem.ts:89-125, 209-263): internal/external classification uses realpath at scan time and can diverge from copy time; internal symlinks are recreated inside agent workspaces; symlink snapshot hashes cover scope+target string, not target content, so snapshot integrity can miss content drift at link targets.

Freeze/copy consistency gap: manifest scan, baseline-hash index generation and workspace copyTree are separate passes over the working copy — concurrent modification can make workspace bytes diverge from the frozen manifest that TargetSpec validation and evidence provenance trust.

Coordinator complexity concentration: packages/run-engine/src/index.ts (1534 lines) plus retest-service.ts (1111) and verification-service.ts (987) concentrate lifecycle ordering, outcome aggregation, cancellation propagation and historical merge/verify compatibility — the most likely location for ordering, double-terminalization or lost-partial-outcome defects.
RPC-timeout reconciliation: the RUN_MAY_HAVE_STARTED path in apps/runtime must not invent completion or create a second run; timeout-vs-actual-start races need code-level verification.

Test-coverage asymmetry: apps/desktop has 48 unit test files while workspace-factory has 1, snapshot-engine 1 and persistence 6 — thin coverage around exactly the containment/path-validation code the security claims rest on.

Shared command router drift: renderer IPC and the external CLI share desktop-command-router with a 'narrower allowlist' — allowlist or argument-validation drift between the two surfaces could expose runtime commands or IDs to the external CLI.

Documented security guarantees not yet code-verified: 'no plaintext persistence fallback' (safeStorage unavailable path), 'credentials stay outside renderer payloads', export/log redaction, and memory-only runtime configuration are claims in README/threat model requiring failure-path verification.

Dependency availability: node_modules is unpopulated in this snapshot, so running the Vitest suite may be infeasible and verification may have to rely on reading test sources instead of executing them (limitation to record).

findings.title: Clean builds and tests fail from the supplied snapshot because generated tsbuildinfo files are shipped
findings.description: The snapshot ships generated TypeScript incremental metadata (`*.tsbuildinfo`) even though .gitignore excludes it. In a clean checkout, `tsc -p` trusts this stale metadata and skips emitting outputs that are absent from the checkout. Observed effects: packages/shared build exited 0 with no dist; packages/schemas produced only primitives.js and no index.js; apps/desktop preload tsc exited 0 with no dist/preload, causing fix-preload.mjs to fail with ENOENT; apps/cli and apps/runtime dist were absent after a forced turbo run. Deleting the tsbuildinfo files and rebuilding emits the missing dist outputs.
findings.expectedBehavior: A clean checkout of the snapshot should run pnpm build and pnpm test without requiring manual deletion of ignored generated artifacts.
findings.actualBehavior: tsc exited 0 but dist was missing or partial, causing build/test failures (TS2307 for @qa/shared or @qa/schemas and ENOENT for dist/preload/package.json) until tsbuildinfo files were removed.
reproductionSteps: Run `pnpm run build` in packages/shared with the shipped tsbuildinfo (op_13) and observe no dist emitted.
Run `npx tsc -p tsconfig.preload.json` in apps/desktop with the shipped tsbuildinfo (op_40) and observe no dist/preload emitted.
Delete the tsbuildinfo files and rebuild (op_19, op_41, op_78, op_82) to observe the missing dist outputs are emitted.
findings.rootCause: The snapshot packages generated TypeScript incremental metadata (`*.tsbuildinfo`) that is ignored by .gitignore. In a new path, tsc -p trusts this metadata and skips emitting outputs that are absent from the checkout.
findings.recommendedFix: Exclude `*.tsbuildinfo` and `dist` artifacts from published snapshots, and add a packaging/pre-build check that fails when ignored generated files are present.

findings.title: Claude Code QA prompt parity test is not hermetic on WSL hosts without a systemd user bus
findings.description: The qa-prompt-parity test constructs ClaudeCodeHarnessAdapter with the `windowsUsersRoot` test seam but does not set `wslMountIsolationOverride`. On this WSL2 host, the adapter's WSL mount-isolation preflight runs and fails closed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any provider turn, so the last adapter event is `run.failed` and the assertion expects `run.completed`. A focused vitest run reproduces the failure, and a node reproduction of the adapter without the override emits run.failed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE and makes 0 prompts. This is correct runtime fail-closed behavior, but the test is environment-dependent.
findings.expectedBehavior: The parity test should pass on any supported host by stubbing the WSL mount-isolation preflight.
findings.actualBehavior: The focused vitest run reports `expected 'run.failed' to be 'run.completed'`; the adapter emits run.failed with code GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any provider prompt.
reproductionSteps: Run `pnpm --filter @qa/harness-claude-code exec vitest run tests/qa-prompt-parity.test.ts` (op_86); it reports 1 failed test.
Run a node reproduction of the adapter without wslMountIsolationOverride (op_51); it emits run.failed with GLM_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE before any prompt.
findings.rootCause: The adapter correctly fails closed when WSL mount isolation is unavailable, but the parity test only stubs `windowsUsersRoot`, not `wslMountIsolationOverride`; on WSL hosts without a systemd user bus the preflight fails before the test's clientFactory is used.
findings.recommendedFix: Add `wslMountIsolationOverride: { status: 'available', reason: 'test-seam' }` to the ClaudeCodeHarnessAdapter options in qa-prompt-parity.test.ts (or otherwise stub the WSL preflight) so the test is host-independent.
